reason: The text explicitly describes the affliction of the Hebrew people in Egypt. God declares: 'I have surely seen the affliction (עֳנִי - oni) of my people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry (צַעֲקָה - tza'akah) by reason of their taskmasters (נֹגְשִׁים - nogsim); for I know their sorrows (מַכְאֹבִים - mak'avim).' The passage further mentions God's intention to deliver them from Egyptian oppression and from the hand of the Egyptians. These explicit references to affliction, outcry under taskmasters, and sorrows directly confirm that the Hebrews are portrayed as an oppressed and persecuted people in Egypt.
